about.title: About Beytak
about.intro: A rental marketplace built for one market rather than adapted to it — where a listing means the same thing every time, and the person on the other end is the owner.
about.whyTitle: Renting here is harder than it should be
about.whyP1: Finding a home in Jordan means trawling Facebook groups and classified ads where no two listings describe the same things. Half omit the floor, most omit the area, and the ones that look right turn out to be taken. A broker wants a month's rent to make introductions, and the dates you agreed by phone were quietly promised to somebody else.
about.whyP2: Beytak fixes the parts of that a platform can actually fix. Every listing carries the same fields. Availability is enforced by the server rather than remembered by a person. The price you agree is the price stored. And the introduction costs nothing, because owners pay a small subscription instead of taking a cut of your rent.
about.imgAlt: A furnished apartment in Amman with the city visible through the window
about.badgeText: One platform for a fortnight in Aqaba and a year in Abdoun.
about.howSub: Four steps from searching to keys in hand.

steps.p: Filter by city, property type, rental period, bedrooms, price and furnishing. Every listing carries the same structured details, so two flats can actually be compared.
Each listing shows the dates already taken before you pick yours, including the gap an owner keeps between tenants. No guessing, no request refused after the fact.
Choose a start date and a duration; we work out the end date and the total. The owner reviews the request, and their number appears once they confirm.
Pay the owner however you both agree — cash, CliQ, bank transfer or card. Beytak records that it happened and takes nothing from it.

guarantees.p: Area in m², floor, building age, furnishing and turnover days are required fields, not optional prose. That is what makes a search result comparable instead of a wall of adverts.
Availability is settled by the server, not the calendar in the browser. The same rule that draws the calendar refuses the booking, so it can never offer a date it would then reject.
A booking stores its total the moment it is created. An owner raising their price later changes nothing about a booking already made.
Owners pay a flat monthly subscription to list. Renters pay Beytak nothing, and the rent never passes through us — you deal with the owner directly.

regions.desc: Modern apartments in Abdoun, Dabouq and Khalda, student studios around University Street, and older flats with character in Jabal Al Weibdeh.
Ottoman stone houses on the slopes below the old town, hillside terraces with valley views, and quiet village homes within reach of the ruins.
Sea-view apartments and short-stay flats by the week, minutes from the public beach and the souq, for a season or a fortnight.
